transcriptText: Ahmed: This is the postmortem for Tuesday's payments outage. Let's reconstruct the timeline first. Dana: The first alert fired at 14:02 when the payments queue depth crossed threshold. Chen: Root cause was a poison message that wedged the consumer; it retried in a tight loop and exhausted the connection pool. Ahmed: Right. Customer impact was roughly eighteen minutes of failed checkouts, about 1,200 transactions. Dana: I pushed the mitigation at 14:20 by purging the poison message and restarting the consumers. Ahmed: Thanks for the fast response. For follow-ups - I'll add a dead-letter queue so poison messages can't wedge the consumer. Chen: I'll add an alarm on the consumer restart count, separate from queue depth. Mara: From a comms angle, the status page wasn't updated until 14:35. I'll write a runbook step so the on-call updates the status page within five minutes. Ahmed: Good. I'll also schedule a game-day to rehearse this failure mode next sprint. Dana: We should backfill the 1,200 failed transactions - finance needs a reconciliation. Ahmed: Agreed, but let's confirm ownership. Chen: I'll own the reconciliation with finance. Ahmed: We agreed this was a Sev1 and that the absence of a dead-letter queue was the biggest gap. Mara: I'll put all the action items in the tracker after this.

actionItems: Add a dead-letter queue so poison messages can't wedge the consumer
Schedule a game-day to rehearse this failure mode next sprint
